candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control → Standard Precautions/Sharps Safety: prevent exposure to bloodborne pathogens through safe handling and disposal of contaminated needles and use of appropriate safety equipment.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — contaminated dialysis-needle sharps safety
candidate.educational_objective: Prevent occupational bloodborne-pathogen exposure after dialysis needle use by activating available sharps-safety features and immediately disposing of contaminated needles without routine recapping, bending, or breaking.

options.A: Activate the engineered sharps-safety feature when present and dispose of the contaminated needle promptly in an appropriate sharps container without routine recapping.
options.B: Recap each contaminated needle with two hands before carrying it across the room to a sharps container.
options.C: Leave used needles on the work surface until the entire dialysis station has been cleaned, then dispose of them together.
options.D: Break or bend the contaminated needle before disposal so it occupies less space in the sharps container.

candidate.rationale: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires engineering and work-practice controls to eliminate or minimize occupational exposure, including appropriate safer medical devices such as sharps with engineered sharps-injury protections. OSHA guidance instructs workers to activate safety features, avoid routine recapping, bending, or breaking of contaminated needles, and dispose of contaminated sharps immediately or as soon as feasible in appropriate puncture-resistant sharps containers. Therefore, A is correct. B uses prohibited routine two-handed recapping, C delays safe disposal, and D uses prohibited bending or breaking of contaminated needles.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports use of safety-engineered sharps and prompt sharps-container disposal without routine recapping, bending, or breaking after contaminated needle use.
candidate.source_document_title: Bloodborne Pathogens — General Guidance; Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention — Quick Reference Guide
candidate.source_locator: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens General Guidance → best practices: use sharps with engineered sharps-injury protection, activate safety features, do not recap/shear/break contaminated needles, and immediately dispose of contaminated needles in secured puncture-resistant sharps containers. OSHA Quick Reference Guide → safer medical devices and engineering/work-practice controls must be used to eliminate or minimize occupational exposure where feasible.
